messages.author: 6db62e08ec862130
messages.subject: promote_args
parts:
Code like this is really horrible to read,

typename boost::math::tools::promote_args<typename scalar_type<TM_sampleMu>::type,
typename scalar_type<TM_sampleSigma>::type,
typename scalar_type<T_loc>::type,
typename scalar_type<TM_covar>::type>

I wonder if we could hide this in macros like,

#define STAN_PROMOTE(t1,t2,t3) \
typename boost::math::tools::promote_args< \
typename scalar_type<t1>::type, \
typename scalar_type<t2>::type, \
typename scalar_type<t3>::type>

?

--

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] promote_args
parts:
Hi Joshua,

1) I agree with what Michael's suggested. There might already be a `return_type` traits program that we haven't been consistent about using.
2) What's horrible to read about it? Once familiar with the types, the way it's originally written is clear: you're promoting to the scalar types of each of the template arguments. If it was hidden behind something that wrapped it, sometimes it's harder to tell if the type is supposed to be a scalar, vector, matrix, etc.
3) I would like to avoid macros. When they work, they're fine. When they break, it gets much harder to find out what caused the error. If we take your earlier questions about instantiating template types and hid the pattern behind a macro, the error message should point to the macro and not to the cause itself. That makes it really hard to debug.

With all that said, I do think we have a `stan::return_type` that should take in t1, t2, t3. Do you want to check for its existence, and if it does exist, create an issue to use it consistently across the math library?


Daniel

parts:
> On Jan 10, 2015, at 12:45 PM, Joshua N Pritikin <jpri...@pobox.com> wrote:

> > Code like this is really horrible to read,
> >
> > typename boost::math::tools::promote_args<typename scalar_type<TM_sampleMu>::type,
> > typename scalar_type<TM_sampleSigma>::type,
> > typename scalar_type<T_loc>::type,
> > typename scalar_type<TM_covar>::type>

It's also missing the final "::type" :-)

I would also rather avoid macros. We could simplify
to this:

typename math::promote_scalar<T_sample_mu,
T_sample_Sigma
T_mu,
T_Sigma>::type

with some very some very simple templates:

namespace stan {

namespace math {

template <typename T>
struct promote_scalar {
typedef
boost::math::tools::promote_args<typename scalar_type<T>::type>::type
type;
};

template <typename T>
struct promote_scalar {
typedef
boost::math::tools::promote_args<typename scalar_type<T1>::type
typename scalar_type<T2>::type>::type
type;
};

...

}

}

We may already have something like that in meta.

There's some ways to simplify this with C++11 traits, but
it's not quite as simple as declaring a variable auto because
return isn't isolated in a single part of the program.

- Bob
